tagline: Down the river towns, Vicksburg to the Louisiana line.
intro: From Vicksburg, high on its bluff above the Mississippi, US 61 runs south more than a hundred miles, alongside the river through Port Gibson and Natchez to Woodville and the Louisiana line. Side roads go off west toward the water, to the ghost town of Grand Gulf and out Rodney Road past the columns of Windsor.

Grant came through this country in the spring of 1863, landing at Bruinsburg and fighting at Port Gibson on May 1 on his way to Vicksburg. Port Gibson's city-limit sign repeats what he is supposed to have said of it, that it was too beautiful to burn.

moments.title: Windsor Ruins
moments.text: Twenty-three columns, 40 feet high with iron Corinthian tops, are what stands of a mansion that got through the Civil War and burned in 1890 from a guest's dropped ash.

moments.title: Rodney
moments.text: In 1817 Rodney came within three votes of being the state capital. Then the river moved off and the railroad went elsewhere. The church keeps a cannonball, a replica, above its windows.

moments.title: Clark Creek Natural Area
moments.text: Thirteen miles west of Woodville, some 50 waterfalls, a few of them dropping 30 feet, come down through the loess ravines of the Tunica Hills.
